frontier.hypothesis: Target's `move a3,a0` is a register-ALLOCATION outcome (a coalescing failure), not a source-structure one, so it cannot be reached by any further read-count or address-spelling sweep.
frontier.mechanism: cse replaces the base's redundant load with a reg-reg copy in every one of our builds too; local-alloc then coalesces it because the two pseudos do not conflict. Target's survive, so target's pseudos must conflict or carry an opposing preference. ~20 read-count spellings and 8 base spellings all failed to change this, which is what a pure-RA property looks like from the C side.
frontier.next_probe: Spend the allocator-dump probe that s1/s2 both banked and never ran: cc1 -da on the 14-form (tools/gcc-2.7.2/cc1 per [[instrumented-cc1-location]], dumps to tmp/grind/func_80017848/s4/) and read .lreg/.greg to see which pseudo pair is coalesced and what conflict or register preference would prevent it. That names the property directly instead of guessing spellings.

frontier.hypothesis: The conflict that keeps target's copy alive comes from loop-1's SKIP edge: in target the blez at insn 36 jumps to .L8001791C, which is loop-2's guard AFTER loop-1's exit reload, so the loop-1 preheader's a0/a1 are live-out along the skip edge and conflict with the base pseudo.
frontier.mechanism: A pseudo that is live-out on one successor edge conflicts with a pseudo defined on the other, so local-alloc cannot coalesce the copy that bridges them. Our build instead gives both paths one shared reload, so nothing is live across and the copy folds. This also explains why target is 127 insns and every one of our forms is 122-125.
frontier.next_probe: Build a C shape where loop 2's guard is reachable from loop 1's skip WITHOUT its own read - e.g. hoist loop 2's count read next to loop 1's, or chain the two guards so the skip of loop 1 falls directly into loop 2's compare - and check whether `move a3,a0` appears and whether the loop-1 exit grows its own `lw a0,0xC(s2); sll a1,s4,6` pair as in target insns 51-52.

frontier.hypothesis: The remaining 2-insn gap is in the regime where decomp-permuter outperforms hand sweeps, and permuter has never been run on this function.
frontier.mechanism: s1-s3 were all hand-authored spelling matrices (~105 forms total) and the last three levers found (do-while shape, guard comparison operand, guard association order) were each invisible until someone happened to write that exact spelling. With 125 of 127 insns byte-exact and both residual insns confined to one basic block, the search space a permuter explores is now tiny.
frontier.next_probe: Seed a fresh-seed campaign from candidate.c per [[permuter-fresh-seed-discipline]] (tools/permuter_campaign.py; wait in-turn with `wait --dir <ws>` and `harvest --stop` before ending the turn per [[grinder-permuter-orphan-stop-gate]]), scoring against the 14 floor.
